gloss: to distract oneself; to take one's mind off something

definitions.gloss: to distract oneself; to take one's mind off something
definitions.explanation: To do something in order to divert one's attention from worry, sadness, boredom, or discomfort.

examples.japanese: {散歩|さんぽ}をして{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らす。
examples.english: I take a walk to take my mind off things.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}を{聴|き}いて{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らした。
examples.english: I listened to music to distract myself.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{結果|けっか}が{気|き}になるが、{料理|りょうり}をして{気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らすことにした。
examples.english: I'm anxious about the exam results, but I decided to cook to take my mind off it.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
This is a set phrase using {紛|まぎ}らす (to divert, to distract). The verb {紛|まぎ}らす conjugates as a godan verb: {紛|まぎ}らさない / {紛|まぎ}らして / {紛|まぎ}らした.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らすために (in order to distract oneself)
- {気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らす{方法|ほうほう} (a way to take one's mind off things)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
{気|き}を{散|ち}らす means to distract in a more general sense (including unwanted distractions). {気晴|きば}らし (diversion, pastime) is the noun form of the same concept.
